findings.reason: Table size/traffic/runtime statistics are unavailable. Lock mode can be described but duration and downtime are unknown.
findings.remediation: Collect labeled metadata and rehearse representative workload; do not invent row counts or timing.

findings.reason: CASCADE can remove recorded dependent objects. The impact paths include potential static consumers too; those are not PostgreSQL's exact cascade deletion closure.
findings.remediation: Review catalog dependency types/internal ownership and explicitly approve each removal. Prefer RESTRICT while investigating.

findings.reason: Constraints/indexes/column-specific triggers depend on the changed object via the displayed edge kinds.
findings.remediation: Rebuild or transition affected objects with verified order and constraint validation.

findings.reason: DROP COLUMN destroys column data and affects known dependency/source references.
findings.remediation: Preserve data and transition consumers before a separately reviewed destructive contract.

findings.reason: Destructive contract lacks evidence of completed application transition.
Known views/routines/SQL consumers reference this object. Catalog paths and parsed source references have distinct guarantees; untracked routine bodies remain UNKNOWN.
findings.remediation: Review the supplied dependency paths and verify runtime consumers; never claim all function calls were discovered.

unknowns.explanation: Catalog dependencies cover recorded edges only; repository/runtime consumers and some object definitions are unavailable.
